description: Role-aware grammar for scripts/ zone. Each .py file must belong to exactly one role family. Roles are mutually exclusive and exhaustive (via 'unclassified').

machine_checks.has_main_guard: if __name__ == '__main__' block present anywhere in file
machine_checks.has_function_or_class: at least one FunctionDef or ClassDef in the AST
machine_checks.has_only_data: no FunctionDef or ClassDef at any level (derived: NOT has_function_or_class)
machine_checks.has_syspath_mutation_at_top_level: sys.path.insert or sys.path.append called at module top level, outside any __main__ guard block
machine_checks.has_sysexit_at_top_level: sys.exit() or SystemExit() called at module top level, outside any __main__ guard block

boundaries.name: import_safety
boundaries.description: Detect top-level side effects that mutate interpreter state on import

boundaries.name: error_boundary
boundaries.description: Detect top-level sys.exit that terminates the process on import

boundaries.name: data_purity
boundaries.description: Detect modules that are purely declarative (no behavior)
boundaries.triggers: declaration_module when import-safe and no functions/classes

runnable_entrypoint.description: Has __main__ guard; callable directly via `python scripts/foo.py`. May import other modules but is not itself meant to be imported.
runnable_entrypoint.notes: Import-safety checks do NOT apply to runnable_entrypoint files. sys.path bootstrapping inside a runnable script is acceptable.

import_safe_support.description: Importable library; no top-level side effects on import. Contains functions and/or classes that callers use. Examples: io_helpers.py, tide_ops.py, ledger_ops.py, tide_parser.py.

required.name: function_or_class
required.description: at least one function or class definition (provides reusable behavior)

excluded.name: main_guard
excluded.description: no __main__ entry point (would make it runnable_entrypoint instead)

excluded.name: only_data
excluded.description: not a pure-data module (would be declaration_module instead)

declaration_module.description: Constants, tables, or schema data; primarily data, no behavior. Contains only module-level assignments and import statements. Example: economy_constants.py.

required.name: only_data
required.description: no function or class definitions at any level

unclassified.description: File doesn't cleanly fit any other role. Explicit reason required. NOT a catch-all — use only when a specific boundary violation is detected. Example: pipeline_parser.py (sys.path mutation at top level, no __main__ guard).

trigger_conditions.name: syspath_import_violation
trigger_conditions.reason_template: sys.path mutation at module top level (import-safety violation)

trigger_conditions.name: sysexit_error_violation
trigger_conditions.reason_template: sys.exit call at module top level (error-boundary violation)

unclassified.notes: The reason field is mandatory. Files in this role should be refactored: move sys.path bootstrapping behind __main__ guard or convert to a runnable_entrypoint.

counterexamples.io_helpers.py: import_safe_support — functions only, no __main__, no side effects
counterexamples.tide_ops.py: import_safe_support — functions only, no __main__, no side effects
counterexamples.tide_parser.py: import_safe_support — dataclasses + functions, no __main__, no side effects
counterexamples.ledger_ops.py: import_safe_support — class + functions, no __main__; try/except import is safe (read-only, no process state mutation)
counterexamples.economy_constants.py: declaration_module — only constant assignments, no functions, no __main__
counterexamples.pipeline_parser.py: unclassified — sys.path.insert at module top level (line 14-15) without __main__ guard; mutates interpreter state on import
